discrepancies.title: OM income AED 1,066,000 vs in-place rent AED 991,000

sources.label: rent roll in-place rent, 24 let units
rent roll in-place rent plus asking rent on 2 vacant units

discrepancies.why: The OM figure is not contracted income: it equals the rent roll's in-place rent plus asking rent on 2 vacant units (AED 1,065,500). The screen underwrites let units at their contract rent and vacant units at the screen reference rent after downtime. Gross yield on price falls from 9.7% to 9.0% on in-place rent.

impact.basis: OM stated income above rent-roll in-place rent

discrepancies.analyst_action: Ask for signed leases or Ejari certificates behind any unit the OM counts as income; treat the rest as vacant.

discrepancies.title: OM yield 9.7% is on asking price, before 6.2% acquisition costs

sources.label: acquisition costs (DLD 4%, broker, trustee, mortgage registration)

discrepancies.why: A buyer pays AED 686,947 on top of the price. On price plus costs the same income gives 9.1%.

impact.basis: OM income on price plus acquisition costs, minus the stated yield

discrepancies.analyst_action: Compare deals on yield on total cost; ask the broker to restate the yield on that basis.

notices.text: Tenants' security deposits of AED 54,500 transfer to the buyer and must be credited at closing.
Cheque profile: 23% of rent on 1-2 cheques, 43% of rent on 3-4 cheques, 33% of rent on 6 or more cheques. More cheques mean more collection risk and less post-dated cheque cover.

diligence_checklist.text: Title deed and DLD ownership search: freehold status, single title, and that the buyer is eligible to own the plot.
Building completion certificate (Dubai Municipality) for the as-built building.
Affection plan and permitted use: confirm residential use and the plot's permitted floors match the building.
Ejari export for every lease, reconciled to the rent roll unit by unit.
Civil Defence completion and annual fire-safety certificates, and ACP cladding compliance.
Building condition survey and capex plan for a building of this age (MEP, lifts, facade, waterproofing).
Retail leases: permitted use, trade licences and VAT treatment of shop rents.

memo.markdown:
## Verdict
**Decline**: the building fails two hard mandate filters. It has 26 units [[om.unit_count]] against a minimum of 30 [[mandate.min_units.threshold]], and an asking price of AED 11.0m [[deal.asking_price_aed]] against a minimum of AED 30m [[mandate.min_price_aed.threshold]]. Nothing else changes that. Returns below are context only and are not decisive.

## The deal
- **What and where:** Tulip Court, International City Phase 1, China Cluster. 26 units [[rr.unit_count]], completed 2009 [[deal.completion_year]], G+3, freehold on a single title.
- **Price:** asking AED 11.0m [[uw.price_aed]], which is AED 817 per sq ft [[uw.price_per_sqft_nsa]] on net area and AED 670 per sq ft [[uw.price_per_sqft_bua]] on built-up area.
- **Income:** in-place contract rent is AED 991k [[rr.in_place_rent_aed]] from 24 let units [[rr.let_units]]. Occupancy is 92% [[rr.occupancy_by_units]] by units and 94% [[rr.occupancy_by_area]] by area, as of 31 October 2026 [[rr.as_of]]. The leases are direct, with no master tenant. The mix is 15 studios [[rr.studio.units]], 1BR units (9 [[rr.1br.units]]) and 2 retail units [[rr.retail.units]].

## Returns
For reference only; not decisive.

| Metric | Result | Mandate |
|---|---|---|
| Unlevered IRR, pre-tax | 1.9% [[uw.unlevered_irr_pre_tax]] | 7.5% [[mandate.target_unlevered_irr.threshold]] |
| Unlevered equity multiple | 1.09x [[uw.unlevered_equity_multiple_pre_tax]] | 1.30x [[mandate.target_unlevered_equity_multiple.threshold]] |
| Going-in net yield on total cost | 5.7% [[uw.going_in_net_yield_on_cost]] | 6.0% [[mandate.min_going_in_net_yield_on_cost.threshold]] |
| Entry yield on price | 6.0% [[uw.entry_yield_on_price]] | none |
| Exit yield | 7.8% [[uw.exit_yield]] | none |

Year-1 NOI is AED 660k [[uw.noi_year1]]. The deal misses both return targets and the yield minimum.

Levered returns are worse. Levered IRR is a loss of 1.1% a year [[uw.levered_irr_pre_tax]] and the levered multiple is 0.95x [[uw.levered_equity_multiple_pre_tax]]. Year-1 DSCR is 1.40x [[uw.dscr_year1]].

The OM headlines a 9.7% yield [[om.yield_stated]] on asking price, with the basis not stated. On the buyer's basis (Year-1 NOI on price plus acquisition costs) it is 5.7% [[uw.om_yield.buyer_net_on_total_cost]], which is 4.0 points [[uw.om_yield.gap_vs_stated]] lower.

## What would make it fail
It already fails the mandate. Even with market rent 5% [[uw.sens.rent_shift_step]] higher and the exit yield 50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] tighter, unlevered IRR is only 4.5% [[uw.sens.r+5.e-50.unlevered_irr_pre_tax]]. With market rent 5% [[uw.sens.rent_shift_step]] lower and the exit yield 50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] wider, it is a loss of 0.7% [[uw.sens.r-5.e+50.unlevered_irr_pre_tax]].

## Discrepancies
Lower-severity items are not discussed.

1. **OM income includes potential rent (high).** The OM's annual rent of AED 1.1m [[om.annual_rent_stated]] is in-place rent plus asking rent on the 2 vacant units [[rr.vacant_units]]. It is not contracted income. The screen used the rent roll, with let units at contract rent. The overstatement is AED 75k [[disc.potential_rent_as_income.impact_aed]]. Gross yield on price falls from 9.7% [[om.yield_stated]] to 9.0% [[uw.gross_yield_in_place_on_price]] on in-place rent.
2. **OM yield ignores acquisition costs (medium).** The 9.7% [[om.yield_stated]] is on asking price, before acquisition costs of 6.2% [[uw.acquisition_costs_pct_of_price]]. On price plus costs, the OM's own income gives 9.1% [[uw.om_yield.stated_income_on_total_cost]]. That is 0.6 points [[disc.yield_excludes_acquisition_costs.impact_ratio]] lower.

## Checks before diligence
None are needed unless the mandate is waived on unit count and price. If it is:
- Ask for signed leases or Ejari certificates behind any unit the OM counts as income. Treat the rest as vacant.
- Ask the broker to restate the yield on total cost.
- Security deposits transfer to the buyer and must be credited at closing.
- Review the cheque profile. More cheques mean more collection risk and less post-dated cheque cover.
- Title deed and DLD ownership search, including buyer eligibility.
- Dubai Municipality completion certificate.
- Affection plan and permitted use.
- Ejari export for every lease, reconciled to the rent roll.
- Civil Defence certificates and cladding compliance.
- Condition survey and capex plan for a building of this age.
- Retail leases: permitted use, trade licences and VAT treatment.

## Assumptions
The results rest on the firm's house view, not on evidence for this building. The exit yield is 7.8% [[uw.exit_yield]], including 25 bps [[assume.exit_yield_expansion_bps]] of expansion. Market rent falls 1.0% [[assume.rent_growth_year1]] in Year 1, is flat in Year 2 (0.0% [[assume.rent_growth_year2]]), then rises 2.0% [[assume.rent_growth_year3]], 3.0% [[assume.rent_growth_year4]] and 3.0% [[assume.rent_growth_year5]]. Structural vacancy is 5.0% [[assume.structural_vacancy]] and collection loss is 1.0% [[assume.collection_loss]]. The loan is 40% [[uw.ltv]] of value at 6.8% [[uw.interest_rate]], sized to a 1.40x [[assume.sizing_dscr]] DSCR. No operating cost categories were filled from mandate defaults.
